claim: #1090 asks v2 to write plugin.json command as bare 'node'; this directly undoes #841's fix.
why: Two factual problems. (1) Wrong file: docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md never mentions #1090, #841, plugin.json, or install at all (grep confirms; the ADR is about hook CPU budget, not install). The actual #1090 text lives only in tickets/v2-issue-map.md:89 and tickets/map-I1.md:14, which are evidence files, not a v2 design doc, and D2 has no entry in docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md, so it is not an accepted owner decision. (2) No real conflict: #1090's given/when/then is scoped to 'install under Homebrew node' only, and its general rule D2 is 'install never writes a version-pinned node path' -- the same anti-pinning principle #841 already serves. #841 (b1cca82d) fixed resolveHookRuntime's liveness check for mise/asdf/nvm so a stale pinned execPath is re-resolved at run time; it did not mandate writing a literal absolute versioned path forever, and a stable 'node' command for the Homebrew install case does not reintroduce the ENOENT-on-upgrade bug #841 fixed for version managers -- they are different install contexts (Homebrew PATH-stable binary vs mise/asdf/nvm per-version dirs). No doc under review actually instructs engineers to hardcode bare 'node' in a way that would re-break #841's liveness guard.
evidence: grep -n -i '1090\|841\|D2' docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md -> no matches in either file; tickets/v2-issue-map.md:89 and tickets/map-I1.md:14 show #1090 scoped to 'Given install under Homebrew node'; git show b1cca82d (cm-main) confirms #841 fixed resolveHookRuntime via liveNodeRuntime() liveness check for mise/asdf/nvm, a different install path shape than Homebrew.
